requirement: Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. An invalid `{req}` directive or role MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
rationale:
**Implementation: correct and marked.** The behaviour looks right, but the tests leave two of the stated rules unexercised.

- `valid_name` (src/lib.rs:659) accepts only non-empty names whose `.`-separated segments are non-empty and contain only ASCII alphanumerics, `_` or `-`. It is marked `{impl}`.
- `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs:471) leaves a `{req}`, `{example}` or `{definition}` fence literal when its name is invalid. It is marked `{impl}`.
- `reference_roles` (src/lib.rs:566) drops invalid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, `{test}` and `{term}` names. It is marked `{impl}`.
- `chapter_namespace` (src/lib.rs:226) strips a leading `reqs` and a trailing `index` or `README` when the path has more than one segment. It is marked `{impl}`.
- `full_requirement_name` (src/lib.rs:460) joins the namespace and the local name. It is marked `{impl}`.
- `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs:256) reports an error for an invalid full name. It is marked `{impl}`.
- I found no other code that parses requirement names without an `{impl}` marker. `config.rs`, `index.rs` and `definition_glob.rs` validate unrelated identifiers.

**Tests: they leave gaps.**
- `chapter_path_prefixes_the_requirement_name` (src/lib.rs:695) covers `requirements.md`, `reqs/foo/bar.md`, and `reqs/foo/README.md` and `index.md` being stripped.
- `invalid_names_remain_literal_and_html_is_escaped` (src/lib.rs:749) covers a `{req}` block with an invalid name staying literal and an invalid `{impl}` reference being ignored. The only invalid input it uses is a name containing a space.
- `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` (src/lib.rs:883) covers an invalid example name (`bad name`) staying literal.
- `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` (src/evidence.rs:1368) covers only a valid full name.

Three gaps remain:
- **Name rules:** No test covers empty segments (`a..b`, a leading or trailing `.`, an empty name). No test covers non-ASCII characters. Both are explicit parts of the requirement. There is no direct `valid_name` unit test and no test that the character classes (digits, `_`, `-`) are accepted.
- **Evidence error path:** The path in `collect_definitions` that reports `invalid … name` is never tested.
- **Namespace edge case:** `reqs/index.md` (a single segment after stripping `reqs`) yields the namespace `index`, and no test or comment settles whether that is intended.

I am judging false because those tests are missing, not because of any defect in the implementation. No FIXME acknowledges the gaps.
